title: Backtest Platforms
author: jacopo613
selftext:
Hello everyone. I'm looking for a baclesting platform to validate some of my ideas. I only have a few strategies in mind to test that also concern the use of past macroeconomic data (e.g. CPI, UR, etc.) So I'm not going to create an EA, I'm just going to understand market behavior and look for edges to support my manual strategy. Which platform would you advise me to use considering that I have a basic knowledge of programming (of course I would join an AI) and considering that I would look for something not too complicated? 

Reading a few posts, I saw Quantconnect, but I don't know if it would suit me.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: QuantConnect fits this, it has FRED data so CPI and unemployment are built in. one trap: test on the number as first published, not the revised one, or the backtest knows things nobody had on release day. I built Quantradin, but it reads price rules on US stocks and options only, no macro series, so QuantConnect is the better start here. are you looking at release days or slower regimes?

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: QuantConnect works, but it can be a lot if you just want to study how markets react to CPI or unemployment releases. A simple Python notebook with AI help is often easier for that. One thing to watch is using the exact release time and the first published number, not the revised one, or the results will look better than they were. Cymetica's Backtest Labs is another place to test an idea against history.
